newsitem.title: PANAMA: Future Panama Canal board to have two more members.
newsitem.headline: Future Panama Canal board to have two more members.

text.p: The Panama Canal's new board of directors to be apppointed this year will have 11 members instead of nine and they will be named to staggered terms of three to nine years to guarantee independence, a top government official said Thursday.

Jorge Ritter, head of the Panama Canal transition team, said the 11-member body would take over control of the 52-mile (84-km) transoceanic waterway after it is turned over from the United States to Panama at noon Dec. 31, 1999.

President Ernesto Perez Balladares will appoint a chairman and nine members of the board of directors "some time this year," he told the Foreign Press Association. One board member will be appointed by Congress.
He said the board would serve terms of three to nine years "to prevent one president, after Perez Balladares, from appointing the entire board of directors at one time."
The board will work alongside the Panama Canal Commission (PCC) to prepare a new set of regulations for the canal which "should be ready in two to three years," he said.
They will have the authority to name the canal administrator "and it is probable that they would name current administrator Alberto Aleman Zubieta."
